hints: Particle $B$ of mass $2m$ is hanging vertically in equilibrium, so the tension is $T = 2mg$.
For particle $A$ of mass $3m$ on the smooth incline, the tension balances the component of weight down the slope: $T = 3mg\sin\theta$.
walkthrough:
Consider the vertical equilibrium of hanging particle $B$ of mass $2m$:
$$T - 2mg = 0 \implies T = 2mg$$

Consider the equilibrium of particle $A$ of mass $3m$ along the smooth inclined plane:
$$T - 3mg\sin\theta = 0$$
$$2mg = 3mg\sin\theta$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Isolate hanging particle $B$ of mass $2m$. Since the system is in static equilibrium, the net vertical force is zero:
$$T - 2mg = 0 \implies T = 2mg$$

Isolate particle $A$ of mass $3m$ on the smooth plane inclined at angle $\theta$. The forces acting along the line of greatest slope are the upward tension $T$ and the downward component of gravitational force $3mg\sin\theta$:
$$T - 3mg\sin\theta = 0$$

Substitute $T = 2mg$ into the equation of equilibrium for $A$:
$$2mg = 3mg\sin\theta$$

Take the inverse sine to determine $\theta$:
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 41.8^\circ$$

hints: Form the equation of motion for particle $B$ accelerating downwards at $0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$: $2mg - T = 2m(0.1)$.
Form the equation of motion for $A$ moving up the slope with acceleration $0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$: $T - 3mg\sin 30^\circ - \mu R = 3m(0.1)$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law vertically downwards to particle $B$ with acceleration $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2mg - T = 2m(0.1)$$
$$20m - T = 0.2m \implies T = 19.8m$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline on particle $A$ to find the normal reaction $R$:
$$R = 3mg\cos 30^\circ = 3m(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 15\sqrt{3}m$$

Apply Newton's second law up the incline to particle $A$ with friction $F = \mu R$ opposing motion:
$$T - 3mg\sin 30^\circ - \mu R = 3m(0.1)$$
$$19.8m - 3m(10)(0.5) - \mu(15\sqrt{3}m) = 0.3m$$
$$19.8m - 15m - 15\sqrt{3}\mu m = 0.3m$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Isolate hanging particle $B$ of mass $2m$. Applying Newton's second law vertically downwards with acceleration $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2mg - T = 2ma$$
Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2m(10) - T = 2m(0.1)$$
$$20m - T = 0.2m$$
$$T = 20m - 0.2m = 19.8m$$

Isolate particle $A$ of mass $3m$ on the rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$. Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find the normal contact reaction $R$:
$$R = 3mg\cos 30^\circ = 3m(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 15\sqrt{3}m$$

Since particle $A$ accelerates up the incline, limiting friction acts down the incline:
$$F = \mu R = \mu(15\sqrt{3}m)$$

Apply Newton's second law along the incline in the uphill direction of motion:
$$T - 3mg\sin 30^\circ - F = 3ma$$
Substitute $T = 19.8m$, $3mg\sin 30^\circ = 3m(10)(0.5) = 15m$, $F = 15\sqrt{3}\mu m$, and $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$19.8m - 15m - 15\sqrt{3}\mu m = 3m(0.1)$$
$$4.8m - 15\sqrt{3}\mu m = 0.3m$$

Divide through by the common factor $m$:
$$4.8 - 15\sqrt{3}\mu = 0.3$$
Subtract $0.3$ from both sides and add $15\sqrt{3}\mu$:
$$15\sqrt{3}\mu = 4.5$$
Divide both sides by $15\sqrt{3}$:
$$\mu = \frac{4.5}{15\sqrt{3}} = \frac{45}{150\sqrt{3}} = \frac{3}{10\sqrt{3}}$$
Rationalize the denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{3}$:
$$\mu = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{10 \times 3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{10}$$

hints: Find the speed $v$ of the particles when $B$ hits the floor: $v^2 = 0 + 2(0.1)(0.8)$.
Once $B$ hits the floor, the string becomes slack. Find the new acceleration of $A$ up the slope under gravity and friction: $3ma = -3mg\sin 30^\circ - \mu R$.
Use $v = u + at$ with final speed $0$ to find the time until $A$ momentarily stops moving up the slope.
walkthrough:
Calculate the speed of the system when particle $B$ strikes the floor after descending $s = 0.8\text{ m}$ with $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$ from rest:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0 + 2(0.1)(0.8) = 0.16$$
$$v = \sqrt{0.16} = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

When $B$ hits the floor, the string becomes slack ($T = 0$). Particle $A$ moves up the slope opposed by both gravity and friction:
$$F_{\text{net}} = -3mg\sin 30^\circ - \mu R = 3ma$$
$$-3m(10)(0.5) - \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{10}\right)(15\sqrt{3}m) = 3ma$$
$$-15m - 4.5m = 3ma \implies -19.5m = 3ma$$
$$a = -\frac{19.5}{3} = -6.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate the time until particle $A$ momentarily comes to rest ($v = 0$):
$$v = u + at$$
$$0 = 0.4 - 6.5t$$
$$6.5t = 0.4 \implies t = \frac{0.4}{6.5} = \frac{4}{65} \approx 0.0615\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
First, determine the speed of the connected particles at the instant $B$ hits the floor. Particle $B$ accelerates from rest ($u = 0$) through a height of $s = 0.8\text{ m}$ with acceleration $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(0.1)(0.8) = 0.16$$
$$v = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
At the moment $B$ lands on the floor, the string goes slack, eliminating the tension ($T = 0$). Particle $A$ now moves freely up the slope with initial velocity $u = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Identify the forces acting on $A$ along the plane during this second phase: the component of gravity down the plane and the kinetic friction force down the plane:
$$F_{\text{gravity}} = 3mg\sin 30^\circ = 3m(10)(0.5) = 15m$$
$$F_{\text{friction}} = \mu R = \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{10}\right)(15\sqrt{3}m) = \frac{3 \times 15}{10}m = 4.5m$$

Apply Newton's second law to particle $A$ in the uphill direction:
$$-F_{\text{gravity}} - F_{\text{friction}} = 3ma$$
$$-15m - 4.5m = 3ma$$
$$-19.5m = 3ma$$
Divide by $3m$ to find the deceleration:
$$a = -\frac{19.5}{3} = -6.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find the time $t$ until $A$ comes instantaneously to rest ($v = 0$):
$$v = u + at$$
$$0 = 0.4 - 6.5t$$
$$6.5t = 0.4$$
Divide by $6.5$:
$$t = \frac{0.4}{6.5} = \frac{4}{65} \approx 0.0615\text{ s}$$
